The right shade, honest claims and regimens that come back

Beauty buyers want help choosing a shade or routine, trust reviews and creators, and come back when a product runs out. We automate shade and skin-type guidance from your own charts, ingredient-accurate listings with claims review, creator workflows with disclosure checks, consented cart recovery and regimen replenishment.

What makes beauty & personal care different

  • Shade and skin-type uncertainty drives abandoned carts and returns of products that cannot be resold once opened.

  • Ingredient lists, cosmetics labeling details and product claims must be accurate on every listing, and claims such as natural or skin results draw ASCI and regulatory scrutiny.

  • Creator and influencer programs run on spreadsheets and DMs, with missing disclosure labels and unclear usage rights.

  • Samples, minis and first purchases rarely turn into full-size regimens because the follow-up is generic.

  • Review requests and reminders go out at the wrong time or to the whole list at once.

Where automation helps beauty & personal care

  • Shade and skin-type quiz

    Recommend shades and routines from your shade charts and ingredient data through a short quiz, without medical advice. Questions about skin conditions go to a trained advisor.

  • Ingredient-accurate listings with claims review

    Draft listings from pack artwork and ingredient lists, block unsupported claims, and route efficacy wording to your regulatory reviewer before publishing.

  • Creator workflow with disclosure checks

    Brief creators from an approved claims sheet, pre-check drafts for disclosure labels and off-brief claims, and track usage rights and sales by creator code.

  • Consented cart recovery

    Follow up abandoned carts only with opted-in shoppers, offering shade help instead of pressure, with the total price shown upfront.

  • Regimen replenishment and sample conversion

    Remind buyers before a product runs out, and follow up sample buyers with usage tips and a full-size option, never a pre-added item.

  • Reviews after real use

    Ask every buyer for a review once they have had time to use the product, and publish reviews unedited under a published moderation policy.

AI catalog enrichment with mandatory-field checks

Turn supplier sheets, pack photos and spec documents into complete, channel-ready listings. AI drafts titles, attributes and descriptions from approved facts, rules check mandatory declarations, and a category owner approves every listing before it goes live.

Fashion & apparel · FMCG & grocery · Beauty & personal care

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Listings are built by hand from supplier spreadsheets and pack photos, so attributes differ across Shopify, Amazon, Myntra and Nykaa, size charts go missing, and declarations such as net quantity, MRP, manufacturer or importer and country of origin are incomplete. Incomplete listings get suppressed by marketplaces and create avoidable complaints.

Trigger

A new SKU, supplier sheet or pack-artwork change is added to the product master sheet or PIM.

How it runs

  1. Collect the source data: supplier sheet, front and back pack photos, size chart or ingredient list, and documents such as the FSSAI license number.
  2. Extract label text and map it to each channel's attribute schema, flagging fields the source does not support instead of guessing.
  3. Check mandatory declarations: manufacturer, packer or importer, generic name, net quantity, MRP inclusive of taxes, country of origin and consumer care details, plus the FSSAI license number and label particulars for food.
  4. Draft titles, bullets and descriptions from approved facts only, and hold unsupported claims such as clinically proven, chemical-free or medicinal benefits for review.
  5. Send each draft to the category owner's approval queue with the source images side by side.
  6. Publish approved listings through channel APIs or each marketplace's bulk-upload template, update the Google Merchant Center and Meta catalog feeds, and log the approver and version.

Human checkpoint

The category or catalog manager approves every new or changed listing. Claims about cosmetics, food or nutrition go to the client's regulatory or legal reviewer before publishing.

Systems it connects

Uses product data, pack images and supplier documents, not shopper personal data. Source files and approved versions are kept with the listing history so every change can be traced. Prompts exclude cost and margin fields, and access is limited to the catalog team.

  • Drafting prompts tied to approved facts and a banned-claims list

  • Feed publishing workflow with a version log

  • Time from SKU creation to live listing
  • Listings suppressed or rejected by marketplaces
  • Drafts accepted without edits

Creator collaboration and ad-disclosure workflow

Run creator and influencer programs from brief to repost with clear records: product seeding, approved claims sheets, disclosure checks, usage rights and sales by creator code. Built for beauty brands, where claims and disclosure draw close scrutiny.

Beauty & personal care

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Creator programs run on spreadsheets and DMs. Briefs drift from approved claims, paid or gifted posts miss disclosure labels, rights for reposting and ads are unclear, and nobody can tie a creator's content to orders. Beauty claims about skin results or natural and Ayurvedic positioning attract ASCI and regulatory attention.

Trigger

A creator is shortlisted for a campaign, or a creator submits draft content for review.

How it runs

  1. Record each creator's profile, agreed fee, past disclosures and consent to be contacted in the creator tracker.
  2. Generate the brief from an approved claims sheet that lists permitted wording and banned claims for each product.
  3. Track seeding shipments and agreed deliverables, and issue unique discount codes or UTM links.
  4. Pre-check draft captions and scripts with AI for the disclosure labels ASCI's influencer guidelines and the CCPA endorsement guidance expect, and for claims outside the approved sheet, then route them to a reviewer.
  5. Record usage rights and their expiry before any repost, whitelisting or paid amplification.
  6. Report orders, revenue and returns by creator code every week.

Human checkpoint

The brand manager approves every brief and final post. Claims about efficacy, skin conditions or ingredients go to the client's regulatory or legal reviewer; AI only flags issues.

Grounded fit, shade and spec advisor

Answer pre-purchase questions on size and fit, shade and skin type, or technical specs using only the brand's own size charts, shade guides, spec sheets and policies. When the answer is not in the approved sources, the assistant says so and hands over to a person.

Fashion & apparel · Electronics & appliances · Beauty & personal care

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Shoppers ask the same questions on WhatsApp and chat: will this fit, which shade suits me, does this inverter AC suit my room and power supply, is this charger compatible with my phone. Slow or inconsistent answers lose the sale and wrong answers create returns. Generic chatbots guess, which is worse.

Trigger

A shopper opens the size, shade or compare widget on a product page, or asks a product question on WhatsApp or web chat.

How it runs

  1. Index approved sources per category: garment measurements, fit notes and return reasons; shade charts and ingredient lists; spec sheets, compatibility tables and installation requirements.
  2. Capture the question and optional inputs through a short quiz, such as height and usual size, skin tone and type, or room size and power supply.
  3. Retrieve matching passages and draft an answer that cites its source and states uncertainty; nothing is answered from model memory.
  4. Give no medical or dermatological advice and no site-specific electrical-safety judgment, such as wiring or load suitability; route those questions to a trained person or the installation partner.
  5. Hand over to an agent with a summary when confidence is low, the shopper asks for a person, or the question concerns stock, price or delivery dates.
  6. Log unanswered questions as content gaps for the catalog team.

Human checkpoint

Category owners approve the knowledge sources and answer style before launch. Agents take over low-confidence, sensitive or out-of-scope conversations, and a reviewer samples transcripts every week.

  • Size, shade or spec-related return reasons
  • Pre-purchase response time

Consented cart and checkout recovery

Follow up abandoned carts only with shoppers who opted in, on the channel they chose, with honest messages: no fake countdowns, no pre-added items, the total price including fees shown upfront, and a clear way to opt out.

Beauty & personal care · Home & furniture

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Many carts are abandoned, but blanket WhatsApp and SMS reminders without opt-in risk blocks, paused templates and DND complaints. Urgency tricks such as fake stock counters, pre-added items or fees revealed late are dark patterns under the CCPA guidelines and erode trust.

Trigger

An identified shopper leaves checkout with items in the cart and holds an active marketing opt-in for email or WhatsApp.

How it runs

  1. Check consent and channel preference, suppression lists, recent purchases and open support tickets before anything is sent.
  2. After the agreed interval, send an approved WhatsApp marketing template or an email with the cart contents, the total price including delivery and COD fees, and the return policy link.
  3. For furniture, offer a consultation or delivery-date check instead of a discount; for beauty, offer shade or regimen help.
  4. Send no more than the agreed number of reminders, and stop at once on purchase, reply or opt-out.
  5. Route replies with questions to an agent inside the 24-hour customer service window.
  6. Report recovered revenue against a holdout group so the incremental effect is measured honestly.

Human checkpoint

The CRM or growth manager approves templates, frequency caps, any offer and the holdout design. The client's legal or compliance owner reviews message wording against the dark-pattern guidelines before launch.

Replenishment, subscription and retailer reorder reminders

Remind consumers when a pack is likely to run out, run subscribe-and-save without traps, turn sample buyers into full-size customers, and let retailers and distributors reorder their usual basket on WhatsApp for a sales rep to confirm.

FMCG & grocery · Beauty & personal care

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Consumables are bought again on a predictable cycle, but brands send generic offers instead of a timely reminder, subscriptions are hard to pause or cancel, and sample buyers are never followed up. On the B2B side, kirana retailers and distributors reorder through calls and photos of handwritten lists that reps re-key.

Trigger

A shopper's estimated run-out date approaches, a subscription renewal is due, a sample was delivered, or a registered retailer sends a reorder message.

How it runs

  1. Estimate run-out per SKU from pack size, usage guidance and the shopper's own repeat interval.
  2. Send a reminder on the shopper's opted-in channel a few days before the estimate, with a one-tap reorder link.
  3. For subscriptions, send a renewal notice with skip, pause and cancel options as easy to use as subscribing was.
  4. For beauty sample buyers, follow up after the trial period with usage tips and a full-size option, never a pre-added item.
  5. For retailers who opted in, send the usual basket on an approved WhatsApp template, accept edits, apply the approved scheme and pass the draft order to the rep or distributor.
  6. Sync confirmed retailer orders to the DMS or ERP and confirm dispatch to the retailer.

Human checkpoint

The CRM manager approves reminder timing and offers. For retailer orders, the sales rep or distributor confirms credit limits, schemes and the final order before dispatch.

Reviews, drops, back-in-stock and lifecycle journeys

Use RFM segments and stated preferences to send the few messages shoppers value: review and photo requests after delivery, back-in-stock and new-drop alerts they signed up for, and reminders for occasions they chose to share, with reviews published unedited.

Fashion & apparel · Beauty & personal care · Jewellery & luxury

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Brands blast the whole list with every sale, which raises opt-outs and hurts WhatsApp quality ratings. Review requests go out before the parcel arrives or only to happy customers, back-in-stock sign-ups are never notified, and jewelry buyers who shared an anniversary date hear nothing until the next sale.

Trigger

Delivery is confirmed, a sold-out size or shade returns to stock, a new collection goes live, a segment changes, or a saved occasion date approaches.

How it runs

  1. Build RFM and preference segments in the warehouse from orders, returns and stated preferences such as size, shade or metal.
  2. Request a review and photo from every buyer a set time after delivery, not only satisfied ones, and publish reviews without changing their meaning.
  3. Notify back-in-stock sign-ups in sign-up order when the exact size or shade returns.
  4. Send new-drop previews to opted-in segments with the real stock position and no fake scarcity.
  5. Send occasion reminders only to buyers who saved the date for that purpose, with an easy way to remove it.
  6. Measure each journey against a holdout and retire messages that do not earn their place.

Human checkpoint

The CRM manager approves segments, frequency caps and copy. A moderator reviews flagged reviews under a published moderation policy, guided by the voluntary BIS standard IS 19000:2022, and never removes a review for being negative.
